root_cause.text: zram_bvec_write_partial() passes its parent bio to zram_read_page(), which for ZRAM_WB slots triggers an asynchronous read that returns before completion, while the caller subsequently uses and frees the page buffer, leading to a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explains that zram_read_page() uses the parent bio parameter to choose the async path; when non-NULL, the read is asynchronous and the caller proceeds with memcpy_from_bvec, zram_write_page, and __free_page on the buffer before the async read finishes, writing into freed memory. The patch fixes this by passing NULL instead of bio, matching the earlier fix in zram_bvec_read_partial().

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a bug where the write bio was incorrectly passed to zram_read_page during partial writes; the read should not be linked to that bio, so pass NULL instead.
intent_record.what: Changed the third argument of zram_read_page from 'bio' to 'NULL' in the zram_bvec_write_partial function.
intent_record.how: The read operation for the existing page now receives no associated bio, which prevents any bio-related processing (such as I/O completion or error handling tied to the write bio) that could have caused unintended side effects during partial write operations.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 4e3c87b9421df497d849ae61aab9762de7f66afb
Author: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Date:   Tue Apr 11 19:14:58 2023 +0200

    zram: fix synchronous reads
    
    Currently nothing waits for the synchronous reads before accessing the
    data.  Switch them to an on-stack bio and submit_bio_wait to make sure the
    I/O has actually completed when the work item has been flushed.  This also
    removes the call to page_endio that would unlock a page that has never
    been locked.
    
    Dr
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows that zram_bvec_write_partial now calls zram_read_page(zram, page, index, bio) with the parent bio removed (line changed from 'ret = zram_read_page(zram, page, index, bio, true)' to 'ret = zram_read_page(zram, page, index, bio)'), and the synchronous read path (zram_sync_read) now uses an on-stack bio with submit_bio_wait to ensure completion, thus eliminating the use-after-free vulnerability.
